summary: Detects a locale/encoding from a parse result. Calls sub_596245 to parse the input string into a format-classification flag byte and an end-of-string pointer; when the classification flag has bit 2 (value 4) set the encoding is the OEM code page (512) and the double parameter is zeroed, otherwise StringParseViaDelegate parses the numeric double and classification bits 1 and 0 (or delegate returns 1 and 2) select the ANSI (128) and Unicode/DBCS (0x100) encodings, which can be OR-ed together. Stores the resulting encoding word at this+0x0, the consumed byte count (end pointer minus input pointer) at this+0x4 and the double at this+0x10, then returns this.

local_names.a1: output result pointer; receives encoding word, byte count and double
local_names.v3: format-classification flag byte produced by sub_596245
local_names.v9: double value parsed from the locale representation

operations.description: Parse the input locale string with sub_596245(v8, &v10, a2, 0, 0, 0, 0), producing the classification flag byte v3 and the end-of-string pointer v10.
If the classification flag v3 has bit 2 (value 4) set, take the OEM encoding path.
OEM path: set the encoding word v2 = 512 and the double v9 = 0.0.
Otherwise parse the numeric double via StringParseViaDelegate(v8, &v9), storing the delegate return value in v4.
If the classification flag has bit 1 (value 2) set or v4 == 1, set the encoding word to 128 (ANSI/SBCS).
If the classification flag has bit 0 (value 1) set or v4 == 2, OR 0x100 into the encoding word (Unicode/DBCS).
Write the encoding word to this+0x0, the double v9 to this+0x10 and the consumed byte count (v10 - a2) to this+0x4.
Return the output pointer a1 (this), as the callers chain the result.
Invoked from sub_58850F and sub_58B077 during CRT locale initialization.

unresolved: The exact meaning of the two StringParseViaDelegate return values (1 and 2) beyond selecting the ANSI/Unicode encodings is established by the CRT layer, not recoverable here.
The OEM/ANSI/Unicode encoding constants (512, 128, 0x100) are caller-visible; their concrete code-page interpretations live outside this function.
The zeroing of the double on the OEM path and its numeric meaning on the parse path are both passed through to the caller unchanged.
